transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 17:45 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Latrobe Head of ML), Samir Patel (Platform Eng), Dr. Kevin Cho (CTO)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on p95 latency targets, concurrency, streaming support, and token/sec benchmarking. Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) for a real-time patient summarization feature. Agreed to run POC benchmarks with sample prompt sets and clarify security/KMS requirements.

Topics:
- Current infra + model stack
- p95 latency targets and tail behavior
- Concurrent sessions / sustained throughput and token/sec needs
- Streaming & partial response handling for UI
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs (cost, isolation, latency)
- Benchmark plan and next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm alex from redwood, and priya's our se, i'll let her jump in for the technical bits later.
[00:06] Marta: hi, thanks, we wanted to use this call to understand latency and throughput tradeoffs, we're doing live patient note summarization so p95 is really important.
[00:12] Priya: great. can you share your targets? are we talking sub-500ms p95 or multi-second?
[00:18] Marta: for short prompts (single paragraph) we need p95 under 600ms ideally, for longer multi-paragraphs p95 under 1.5s acceptable but less than 2s is required.
[00:28] Dr. Cho: and concurrency, we expect about 150 concurrent users during peak clinic hours, average session 4 requests/min but bursts up to 400 concurrent for batch post-clinic processing, which can be async.
[00:45] Samir: just to add, we stream partial results into the UI so token-by-token latency matters, we can't wait until full generation completes for the UX.
[00:53] Priya: ok that's helpful. streaming is supported on hosted api, we also have options on Dedicated to run with lower jitter and reserved capacity which helps p95. question - are you open to quantized model variants or do you need fp16/ full precision?
[01:06] Marta: we care about output quality - medical accuracy - so we prefer fp16 or higher; quantization ok if you can demonstrate parity on our evals.
[01:15] Alex: right. typical pattern we see: hosted api is quickest to start, but Dedicated gives predictable throughput and reduced p95 jitter because you reserve GPU pools. Private (VPC / on-prem) for strict data residency.
[01:27] Samir: can you give rough token/sec numbers per GPU for small-ish models? like 7B/13B/70B ranges?
[01:33] Priya: rough, for a typical 13B OPT-like transformer on an A100 class node you might see 200-600 tokens/sec single-streaming depending on seq len and kv cache reuse; 7B higher, 70B lower. for p95 we care about tail - batching and cache hit rate impact it.
[01:47] Marta: that variance is big. what controls do you give to tune batching? we can't let long batch queue hurt p95.
[01:54] Priya: we expose batching windows and max batch size per route; we also have latency SLO policies: you can set a hard latency cap so requests that would exceed it will be routed to a lower-cost or lower-capacity fallback or return partial. continuous batching is workload-aware - short requests are partially prioritized, and KV/prefix cache avoids repeated compute.
[02:14] Samir: do you have token/sec benchmarks we can run? we want to measure p50/p95/p99 and token/sec with streaming on/off.
[02:21] Priya: yes, we'll share a benchmarking spreadsheet + harness. typical POC: you give sample prompts, seq len distribution, and concurrency profile; we run tests across hosted and dedicated configurations (single-node, 2-node pool) and provide CSV of latencies and token throughput.
[02:37] Dr. Cho: what about cold-starts and kv cache warmup, will first-run p95 be worse?
[02:42] Priya: yes first-run is worse. we usually prewarm caches for dedicated pools for steady-state. for hosted, warmup depends on recent traffic; we can pre-warm during POC.
[02:51] Alex: also network and region matter - if you're in us-east and model is in eu-west you'll see +50-100ms. Samir, what infra are you using?
[02:58] Samir: our cluster is on AWS, VPC in us-east-1, we prefer agents to be in same region. do you support private deployment in our VPC?
[03:05] Priya: yes, Redwood Private supports a customer-managed control plane with VPC peering and private endpoints. for on-prem we can ship the runtime but that requires more work.
[03:14] Marta: for compliance we need SOC2 + audit logs, key management, and token retention policy - can you confirm?
[03:20] Alex: we have SOC2, KMS integrations (customer-managed keys), and configurable data retention. we'll share the security pack.
[03:26] Marta: good. for the POC can you run two profiles: 1) low-latency profile - Dedicated single-node tuned for p95 600ms for short prompts at 150 concurrent; 2) high-throughput profile - 2-node pool targeting 1000 tokens/sec sustained for batch jobs.
[03:39] Priya: yes we can. couple clarifying q's: what is your average token length per request and the percent of streaming vs non-streaming?
[03:45] Marta: average 60 tokens for short, 240 for long, about 70% streaming (UI flows) and 30% batch.
[03:54] Priya: ok that helps. also are you using any function-calling or heavy sampling? beam search?
[03:59] Samir: no beam search, deterministic sampling with temperature 0.2, and occasional function-like structured outputs.
[04:06] Priya: great, sampling low helps latency. we'll use these parameters in the harness.
[04:11] Alex: on pricing note - Hosted is usage-based, Dedicated is reserved capacity monthly with burst options; we'll send ranges. for decision criteria, is predictability and isolation key?
[04:21] Dr. Cho: predictability and auditability. if Dedicated can meet p95 under 600ms with your config and integrate with our KMS, it's preferred.
[04:30] Marta: also curious about per-route throttling and fallback - if we hit capacity can Redwood fallback to lighter model automatically?
[04:36] Priya: yes we support model variants and automated fallback policies by route - you can set routing by latency, cost, or region.
[04:44] Samir: latency SLO enforcement - can we fail fast if queueing would push us past SLO?
[04:49] Priya: yes you can set 'max-queue-latency' and requests that would go over are rejected or routed. we also expose metrics for queue depth and per-route p95.
[04:58] Marta: what's typical p99 behavior? we're sensitive to tail.
[05:02] Priya: p99 often 2-3x p95 in noisy shared hosted systems; Dedicated tuned for latency tends to reduce that ratio significantly. we'll show p50/p95/p99 in POC results.
[05:12] Alex: ok let's recap next steps - we'll share pricing, security docs, and the benchmark harness. you'll provide prompts and concurrency profile; we'll schedule a 2-hour POC kickoff to run the tests.
[05:21] Dr. Cho: thanks, one more thing - can Redwood support direct KMS integration so keys never leave our control?
[05:27] Alex: yes customer-managed KMS/HSM supported for Private and Dedicated; Hosted can be customer-managed KMS for data encryption at rest. we'll include details.
[05:36] Marta: perfect, thanks.
[05:38] Alex: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites and artifacts.
